primary_target_read.content: KP2.17 full statement and remarks read from primary author PDF via web PDF parser. Workshop summary URL checked separately and does not contain the operative problem.

exact_target: For a nonnegative geodesic current c and a closed geodesic gamma on a hyperbolic surface S, if ell_X(c)=ell_X(gamma) for every hyperbolic metric X on S, must c be a finite convex combination of closed-curve currents? Source leaves surface/metric conventions unspecified. No simplicity restriction appears.
hypotheses_to_audit: nonnegative Radon current rather than a signed distribution
all hyperbolic metrics in a declared topology/metric scope, not finitely sampled metrics
closed geodesic allowed self-intersection and powers
finite convex combination with coefficients summing to one, not arbitrary positive cone or weak closure
closed versus cusped finite-area versus other complete metrics distinguished
continuity/compactness/theorem imports proved with exact domain
success_criteria: Full solution requires classification for the stated domain, or an explicit exotic current with full all-metric length identity and proof that it is outside finite convex hull.
Valid partial requires each restricted theorem and construction proved under exact declared hypotheses, finite diagnostics identified as finite evidence, UNSOLVED maintained.
Closure validation requires all bytes manifested, exact paths/roots and qualified foreign records, every JSON parsed or individually explained pinned deliberate malformed input.
boundary_cases: zero signed differences versus positive currents
provisional_theorem_plan: Derive linear convexity of the equal-length fiber from current intersection with Liouville currents.
Check any countable dense-metric reduction uses continuity, and compactness uses a filling proper length functional on the closed-surface domain.
For simple gamma test measured-lamination or simple-curve rigidity routes without extending them to nonsimple gamma.
Seek direct trace identities or extremal arguments and treat unsupported signed-kernel positivity transfers as blocked.
Independently audit full receipts and original computations with private controls if a concrete defect warrants execution.
